Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2, a hosting platform's customer dashboard with a light/dark theme system: `html[data-theme="light"]`, tokens in app/globals.css). This is a WRITE task based on real, hands-on bug reports from the site owner testing the live site. Fix each precisely, matching the codebase's existing terse comment style.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT — read before touching anything: components/nx/RackHero.tsx and components/nx/Ribbons.tsx (the dashboard's aurora ribbon-stream background) were explicitly reverted to their original state after repeated "fixes" made them worse, per direct owner instruction. Do NOT touch these two files under any circumstances.

ALSO IMPORTANT CONTEXT: a fix was JUST made (moments ago, already in the working tree, don't redo it) to app/layout.tsx and components/nx/ThemeToggle.tsx that gates light mode strictly to /dashboard routes — light mode can no longer leak onto marketing/login pages. That fix is done; your job is the two items below, which are dashboard-internal.

1. **Light mode text colors for support tickets are wrong/unreadable.** Find the support ticket pages (app/dashboard/support and its components — likely components/customer/support-related files or components/nx equivalents) and check every text element's color in light mode: ticket list rows, subject/priority/status badges, message bubbles, timestamps. Compare against how the site owner described it: dark-mode support page looks correct with a purple accent bar and readable white text on dark backgrounds; light-mode broke this (probably similar to the VerifyEmailBanner/ImpersonationBanner contrast bug already fixed elsewhere this session — check if the SAME root cause applies here: a hardcoded dark background with theme-flipping text color, or a `.nx-dark-island` scoping gap). Fix any element where text becomes low-contrast or invisible in light mode.

2. **Scrolling down on a page reveals white space underneath the sidebar in light mode.** This means the sidebar/nav rail (components/nx/Shell.tsx) has a background that doesn't extend far enough — probably a fixed-height background that doesn't cover content once you scroll the main content past a certain point, revealing whatever is BEHIND/BELOW the sidebar's own background (likely body's or a container's background peeking through a gap). Investigate Shell.tsx's sidebar/rail markup and its CSS (search for `.nx-dark-island` and whatever wraps the sidebar) to find why its background doesn't cover the full scrollable height, and fix it so the sidebar's dark background is always fully opaque and full-height regardless of scroll position or content length, in BOTH themes but this specifically manifests in light mode because the "gap" behind it is now light instead of a similar dark shade.

After each fix, run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` and resolve any type errors. Take a screenshot if you have Playwright access to confirm the fix visually before reporting (use `node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/support /dashboard` if credentials work, but don't block on this if it's not straightforward — code-level correctness is the priority). Do not touch RackHero.tsx or Ribbons.tsx. Do not commit — leave changes unstaged. Report back file-by-file with line numbers and what you changed.

Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

#!/bin/bash
# Rebuild and restart the v2 sandbox.
#
# The tree runs a PRODUCTION build (`npm start`), not the dev server: ~0.8 GB
# instead of ~4.5 GB, on a box whose spare memory is measured against fifteen
# customer VMs. The cost is that nothing hot-reloads — every change needs this.
#
# WHY IT STOPS THE SERVER FIRST. `next build` writes into `.next`, which the
# running server is reading from. Building underneath a live server replaces the
# manifests it has open and every route starts returning 500 — this has already
# happened once in this tree. Stop, build, start. Never build in place.
set -euo pipefail

cd /opt/nxeon-v2
LOG=/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log

# ── one build at a time ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two concurrent runs write the same `.next` and corrupt it — the exact failure
# this script exists to prevent, arrived at from a different direction. It was
# survivable only by accident: the build runs inside a transient scope, and
# systemd refuses a second scope of the same name, so run two and the LOSER
# fails loudly. Relying on that is relying on a side effect of a name. This
# takes a real lock and says plainly what happened.
exec 9>/tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock
if ! flock -n 9; then
  echo "==> another rebuild is already running (holding /tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock)."
  echo "    Wait for it to finish — starting a second one would corrupt .next."
  exit 1
fi
